Shared Claude global state requires engine-wide serialization unless config directories are isolated, while provider quota and machine-wide endpoint limits must be shared across codex and claude routes through the same plan_key. Current grouping cannot enforce both.
findings.trigger: A panel runs GLM through claude and the same z.ai plan through codex concurrently, or roster parallel raises claude concurrency.

evidence.observation: Scheduling merges claude labels with a synthetic engine:claude scope, while other endpoint grouping merges provider fingerprints.
Machine-wide running counts are keyed by exact endpoint state, not a shared plan scope.
Different endpoint URLs do not isolate shared ~/.claude state and do not prove shared quota limits are coordinated.

findings.verification: Run two claude children with raised parallel and inspect shared config integrity, then run codex and claude routes sharing plan_key while one is at the provider limit and require one shared waiting group.
findings.remedy: Keep engine-wide claude serialization until per-entry CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolation passes race tests; add plan_key to scheduling and machine health so route limits apply across routes.

evidence.observation: Thirty pairs are suitable for large cost effects, not tight quality parity.
Harness detection records version only, while argv hardcodes restricted, schema, and max-turns flags.
Current terms, retention rules, aliases, and provider event shapes are not verified in this read-only review.

findings.verification: Run a versioned capability smoke per CLI and endpoint before the A/B, then run 30 paired trials and extend toward 100 pairs whenever cost or quality confidence intervals cross the gate.
findings.remedy: Treat 30 pairs as a pilot, pre-register thresholds, extend marginal cases, validate structured output locally, add capability smoke tests, and record a dated terms and data-handling attestation.

findings.claim: Endpoint-mode billing proof has a hole for subscription-servable model ids: the endpoint branch of Get-ClaudeInitProblem rejects only apiKeySource ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and the open endpoint id pattern permits claude-* ids, so an endpoint entry pinning a model the claude.ai subscription can serve has no per-turn proof of non-use - a silent same-model fallback to the local login would be indistinguishable in the ledger. For third-party-only ids (glm-5.3, mimo-v2.6-pro, k3) the init-model equality closes this, and P11 shows no fallback when the token is set; the claim is narrower than F18-1's.
findings.trigger: A roster endpoint entry whose model is a claude-* id (or alias shape) runs on a machine with an active claude.ai login.

evidence.observation: Endpoint branch returns after rejecting only apiKeySource ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; any other value (including 'none', also the subscription's value) passes.
Get-ClaudeModelProblem -Auth endpoint accepts any id matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}(\[1m\])?$ - including claude-sonnet-5-5.
P11: a wrong token yields 401 with no fallback; P8: apiKeySource none with a live login present - the observed token path is proven, the same-model fallback is not.
The documented billing proof ('init.model equal to the pinned id - a subscription turn cannot serve it') holds only when the pinned id is not subscription-servable.

findings.verification: Add the validator refusal, then a harness ENDPOINT check that an endpoint entry with model claude-sonnet-5-5 (or opus) is refused with a clear text; alternatively run RC1 and pin the observed token-source value as the only accepted one.
findings.remedy: In Get-ClaudeModelProblem's endpoint branch, refuse ids that match the Claude model table or alias shape (anything Test-ClaudeModelMatch would accept for the subscription), with a message naming the reason (billing proof); one line plus one harness check.

reviewer_checks.note: E11 rejects closed-table aliases and all claude-* endpoint IDs; direct and mixed-roster refusal replays passed.

findings.claim: Concurrent claude engine instances sharing the same global ~/.claude state directory may still encounter race conditions during config or transcript writes.
findings.trigger: Running multiple claude engines concurrently in a panel without isolated config directories.

findings.remedy: Add explicit file locking around ~/.claude access or enforce per-turn isolated config directories.

findings.claim: Endpoint-mode turns cannot prove they did not bill the local subscription: init apiKeySource 'none' is the expected value on the endpoint route (P8/P10) and also the subscription's value, and the adapter explicitly records it raw and fails only on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — so a silent same-model fallback to the signed-in login is indistinguishable in the ledger.
findings.trigger: A machine with an active claude.ai login runs an endpoint roster entry and the CLI silently prefers the login while serving the same model id.

evidence.observation: Endpoint branch returns early: only an init apiKeySource of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fails the turn; any other source (including 'none') passes, with the comment that 'none' on this route 'proves nothing'.
Turn-outcome model proof for endpoint uses exact equality against the pinned id, so a fallback serving the same model id passes the model check too.

Endpoint credential check is local-only (variable set + URL parses); no per-turn network or header proof exists. The live smoke (ledger n=8) shows apiKeySource none with the token env present, which is consistent with both routes.

findings.verification: Run RC1 and require the recorder to show the request carried the endpoint token (never the OAuth token) with the observed apiKeySource value.
findings.remedy: Before acceptance, run one local Anthropic-compatible recorder proof per CLI version (token + base_url alongside a signed-in config; capture the Authorization header and init apiKeySource), and either fail closed on the ambiguous source or require an endpoint model id that the subscription cannot serve. Record the observed source value as the only accepted one.

findings.claim: A turn that does auxiliary work under a different model can still be accepted as usable: models appearing in assistant events or as non-main modelUsage keys are collected into OtherModels and demoted to a warning, while only init models and the main modelUsage key fail the turn.
findings.trigger: A turn whose assistant events or secondary modelUsage keys name a model outside the pinned id/family but whose init and main model match.

evidence.observation: Init-model drift over all init models and main-model mismatch both fail as capability, but the combined list of remaining modelUsage keys plus assistant models is assigned to OtherModels and only appended to Warnings before Ok=true.

findings.verification: Feed the adapter a stream with matching init/main model plus an assistant message.model of another family and require a capability failure (RC2-adjacent unit check).
findings.remedy: Fail the turn (class capability) on any model outside the pinned match (exact for endpoint, family for subscription/api-key), or document the helper-model allowlist with evidence that helpers cannot bill or act outside the pinned route.

findings.claim: Timeout handling bypasses init capability validation, allowing a later successful continuation to erase evidence that an earlier turn advertised prohibited tools or MCP servers.
findings.trigger: The main turn emits an init containing Bash or an MCP server, makes no monitored tree changes, then times out; its continuation emits an otherwise valid answer.

evidence.observation: An init with tools Read,Bash and MCP server rogue, evaluated with a timeout Pre value, returned an empty failure Class and a resumable ThreadCandidate.
The Pre branch returns before Get-ClaudeInitProblem runs.

Continuation eligibility uses the killed-turn classifier; successful continuation replaces the outcome and clears prior failure fields. That classifier explicitly preserves only auth/quota adapter classes.

findings.verification: Run RC1's prohibited-init timeout case and assert that no continuation launches and the consultation remains failed despite a prepared valid continuation response.
findings.remedy: Validate available init/model evidence before the timeout return, preserve invariant failures across turns, and explicitly prohibit continuation after permission, capability or credential-proof violations.

findings.claim: The largest-output-token heuristic does not enforce one primary model per thread: a different model can produce the final assistant answer while the turn is accepted under the pinned model.
findings.trigger: Init names claude-sonnet-5-5, a top-level assistant answer names claude-opus-5-5, and result.modelUsage reports Sonnet outputTokens 100 and Opus outputTokens 10.

evidence.observation: Get-ClaudeTurnOutcome returned Ok=true, Outcome='usable reply', ModelResolved='claude-sonnet-5-5', and OtherModels containing claude-opus-5-5.
MainModel is selected by maximum outputTokens; differing assistant models are only reported as possible helpers.

findings.verification: Replay a matching init followed by a different top-level assistant model with fewer output tokens and require a capability failure.
findings.remedy: Validate primary assistant events against the resolved pin. Permit helper models only when event provenance identifies them as helpers; do not infer primary-model identity from token volume.

findings.claim: Missing capability fields are accepted as proof of an allowed toolset and no MCP servers, so an incomplete or changed init schema can produce a usable consultation without the claimed evidence.
findings.trigger: An otherwise valid init omits tools and mcp_servers, followed by a successful result.

evidence.observation: Removing both fields produced Ok=true and Outcome='usable reply'.
Missing fields default to empty arrays; validation checks only for extra tools and nonempty MCP lists.

findings.verification: Replay missing, null and wrongly typed capability fields on each init and require an explicit proof failure.
findings.remedy: Preserve field presence and types for every init, require valid capability arrays, and check the expected tools for the selected transport. Treat absent evidence differently from an explicitly empty MCP list.

findings.claim: A rejecting rate-limit event is discarded from the outcome when the terminal result is successful, contrary to the stated rejection rule; the resulting usable record cannot propagate that quota rejection to its plan.
findings.trigger: A stream contains rate_limit_info.status='rejected' with a reset time, followed by subtype success, is_error=false and nonempty output.

evidence.observation: The adapter returned Ok=true, an empty Class and 'usable reply' despite parsing the rejecting event.
Quota evidence selects a failure class only on failure branches; the success branch neither fails nor warns for rejected status.
Health selection treats the latest usable record as clearing quota evidence.

findings.verification: Replay the rejection-plus-success stream through outcome and health classification and assert the documented quota behavior, including its reset time.
findings.remedy: Either make rejecting events terminal as D6 specifies, or define and validate an explicit recovery rule while preserving unresolved quota evidence independently of reply usability.
